title: Query-efficient distance amplification for non-adaptive locally decodable codes

license.adaptation_notice: Faithful editable transcription of the official CCC2021 CC BY4.0 publication, article1 pp1:1--1:57. This item collects the non-explicit distance-amplification main result Theorem72, complete Section6.1 construction and Section6.2 analysis including Proposition65 and full Claims66--71 proofs, Section6.2.1 complete proof and low-error/direct-instantiation discussion, Definition64, and supporting sampler Definition14/Theorem15 full author proof sketch/Lemma16 plus standard Theorem18. Original wording and indices, including Claim68 k3 and Claim69 v notin Bz, are preserved without mathematical correction. Author nonadaptivity, alphabets, constant rate/error, sampler degree conventions and all query/error dependencies retained. Explicit variants Sections6.3--6.6 are outside this item; the complete official original is preserved. core_obligations: Preserve non-adaptive code definition, alphabet, constant-rate/error premise and exact query complexity in Theorem72.
Retain complete encoding/query/reconstruction construction and sampler hypotheses.
Retain all Claims66--71 author proofs and final probability/error deduction in Proposition65.
Retain full sampler15 proof sketch and Theorem72 parameter/error-reduction proof.
difficulty_reason: The author combines three code layers through an unbalanced sampler and traces induced corruption backwards using seven dependent error sets/claims; the reduction couples right-degree control and error amplification to obtain subpolynomial distance overhead. This is a nonroutine coding and probabilistic mechanism.
